final_recommendation: The room converged on a negotiated settlement: FINMA commits to publishing a governance-exoneration statement by April 28th (pre-released April 26th) confirming the write-down was contractually permitted and boards acted reasonably; bondholders withdraw ultra vires filing and issue a Friday public notice signaling closure; D&O carriers close reserves by May 12th. AT1 spreads reprice 150-200 bps wider as permanent floor, not pre-March levels.
minority_objections: Bondholder counsel initially pushed scorched-earth ultra vires litigation as leverage, arguing a five-year discovery war would force regulatory concessions
Two of six D&O carriers held out modeling derivative/regulatory-sanction exposure as a second tail vector not addressed by FINMA's governance finding
key_conflicts: Bondholder counsel vs. institutional investors: litigation-as-leverage vs. orderly repricing to stabilize AT1 market
Insurance carriers vs. bondholder group: whether FINMA's governance finding closes all tail vectors or leaves derivative/sanction exposure live
FINMA vs. bondholders: whether statement language must say 'contractually permitted' vs. merely 'regulatory authority justified'
key_concessions: FINMA agreed to explicit 'boards acted reasonably under emergency circumstances' language in April 28th statement, not just regulatory-authority defense
Bondholders withdrew ultra vires filing entirely (not suspended) contingent on carrier reserve closure by May 12th
Institutional investors accepted 150-200 bps permanent AT1 repricing as new floor, abandoning hope of return to pre-March spreads
Bondholder counsel agreed not to file separate protective notice on derivative vector, treating it as shareholder risk outside AT1 scope
red_lines: Bondholders: FINMA statement must say write-down was 'contractually permitted under explicit viability-event language' — not just 'we had authority'
D&O carriers: will not close reserves unless FINMA explicitly confirms boards' pre-write-down governance was reasonable, not just ordinance validity
Institutional investors: will not re-enter AT1 unless carriers issue written reserve closure by May 12th, not just FINMA's statement
Bondholder counsel: if carriers hedge after April 28th statement lands with promised language, will file ultra vires on carriers' bad-faith reserving
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Shareholder derivative claims and regulatory-sanction exposure as separate tail vectors not closed by FINMA's governance finding
Permanent 150-200 bps AT1 repricing treated as 'orderly' but represents structural damage to bank capital costs across sector
Two carriers still modeling options after April 28th — risk they use 14-day window to extract further concessions or drag into Q2
Bondholder counsel's Friday public notice may move spreads before carriers actually commit in writing, creating false closure signal
downstream_risk_variables: Whether two holdout carriers actually close reserves by May 12th or use derivative/sanction vector to justify extended tail
Market reaction to 150-200 bps permanent AT1 repricing: does it stabilize or trigger further contagion across European bank capital structures
Shareholder derivative litigation risk against boards not addressed by FINMA's governance finding
Reinsurance accumulation if carriers' reserve closure is partial or hedged rather than full withdrawal
Precedent effect on future bank resolutions: does hierarchy inversion become normalized or does this settlement contain it to Credit Suisse
uncertainty_notes: The settlement hinges on three sequential dependencies: (1) FINMA delivers exact governance language by April 26th, (2) two holdout carriers close reserves by May 12th without invoking derivative vector, (3) market accepts 150-200 bps repricing as stable floor rather than contagion trigger. If any link breaks, ultra vires filing resumes and five-year tail reopens. Derivative/sanction exposure remains unresolved second vector.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Ultra vires filing was prepared and used as leverage throughout, but ultimately withdrawn in exchange for FINMA's governance statement — litigation was serious threat but not executed, hence medium not strong
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: Room built substantive challenge to FINMA's legal basis (ordinance vs. contract language, governance reasonableness) but ultimately accepted FINMA's authority once explicit contractual-permission language was secured — developed but not dominant
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion (equity preserved, AT1 wiped) drove the entire negotiation — permanent 150-200 bps repricing explicitly attributed to precedent damage, and settlement structured around containing contagion from this inversion
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 market repricing (150-200 bps permanent widening, carrier reserve behavior, contagion risk across six banks) was central driver of settlement urgency and shaped every concession — room repeatedly returned to spreads/confidence as decision variable
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Multi-year D&O tail (six boards, carrier reserve behavior, May 12th closure deadline, derivative vector as second tail) was developed in granular detail and drove settlement structure — insurance observer's interventions shaped key concessions
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O carrier exposure (reserve closure, reinsurance exhaustion, director premium shocks, two-carrier holdout modeling derivative vector) was concrete, structured, and drove settlement timeline — insurance observer was active shaper of terms
